question.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola with Vertex at the Origin Given a Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096038/assets/5746a438eccdd55d345f1c71a768f971aa1a342798743e151f7557102ddd8783.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(1,-3).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(1,-3),$ we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=-3$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ (-3)^{2} & =4p(1) \\ 9 & =4p \\ p & =\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{9}{4})x \\ {y}^{2} & =9x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{9}{4}$ is positive.
